coaching.headline: A lost Fangtooth and two lost towers between minute 20 and 23 got answered by four straight fight wins, closing it out 10 towers to 3.
coaching.team: The draft put two of five into a lane flagged as their bottom-two: Cuban Noobster into midlane and Mr_Meat31 into support. The comp leaned 3 physical and 2 magical against an opponent running 2 physical and 3 magical, with a frontline and one healer on each side. Lane phase was uneven. The offlane won its lane the entire game and took first blood on Crunch at 3.7. The jungle read favored us early before settling even. The carry lane ran the other way early before Kira took it over late. The support lane was lost to Muriel the entire game. The midlane was lost early too, before settling even. The midlane was also caught alone by Neon three times before minute 10. The first of those deaths, at 4.9, fed straight into the enemy Fangtooth taken at 5.4. The game turned rough between minute 20 and 23. The fight at their Fangtooth, lost 0-2, went out while the offlane sat ahead in its own lane and the midlane stayed alive — neither joined. The follow-up fight at our outer tower, lost 0-3, went out with the offlane absent again and the support pinned in a losing lane. Those two losses gave up a Fangtooth and two outer towers. From the fight at 23.6 on, every fight the team took was won. The biggest came at our inner tower at 27.5, four kills to one, which immediately turned into the Orb Prime. The team closed out both inhibitors and the core inside the next four minutes. It finished 10 towers to the opponent's 3, and more than tripled the opponent on objective damage, 60,725 to 19,340, despite finishing with fewer wards placed than the opponent, 52 to 61. The focus for next game: when a lane is ahead and a fight starts at a contested objective, get that lane into the fight before the count goes 0-3.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The turning point was the double loss between minute 20 and 23. The fight at their Fangtooth, lost 0-2 at 20.2, went out while the offlane sat ahead in a won lane and never joined, and the enemy took the Fangtooth soon after. The next fight, lost 0-3 at our outer tower at 22.1, cost two towers while the support stayed pinned in a lost lane and the offlane again never joined. Every fight from 23.6 onward was won, and two of those wins were cashed directly into the Primal Fangtooth and the Orb Prime, which is what put the game away.
coaching.whatWorked: The clearest strength was the offlane lane win. Greystone took first blood on Crunch at 3.7, held the lane the entire game per the lane read, and finished 3 kills, 1 death, 5 assists — the only player on the roster with just one death across the whole match.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324's Kira led the roster with 14 kills against 3 deaths, and put up the team's highest damage to heroes, 48,265, in a carry lane that started unfavored against GRIM.exe before Kira took it over late. Two of those three deaths were costly rather than careless: the 20.4 death fed the enemy Fangtooth, and the 22.1 death fed two outer towers. Both came in fights the macro read already flags as team-wide numbers losses, with the offlane sitting out a lane it was winning and the support pinned in one it was losing — not solo mistakes. From the fight at 23.6 on, Kira scored in every winning fight the team took, closing the game with more kills than anyone else in the match.

Five deaths were the story of the back half, three of them landing in the same 20-to-24 minute stretch that gave up the Fangtooth, two outer towers, and the Genesis Core. Only three items were completed by the end, the fewest on the roster, the direct cost of dying into those fights instead of farming through them.

22.1.call: This fight was lost 0-3 at our outer tower with two players never in it: the offlane, up in a lane it was winning, and the support, still pinned in its own losing lane. The offlane being ahead meant a shove-and-rotate could have brought another body into the fight; with the support unable to help either, the better call was skipping this fight and resetting for vision or farm instead. Two outer towers fell right after it.

23.6.call: This fight was won 3-1 at their outer tower with four of the five in it — the support was the only one still pinned in its lost lane. The numbers were finally right, and the win should have walked straight into the tower or the next objective; instead it took more than two minutes before an outer tower fell. Winning the fight isn't the finish line — press the structure while the numbers advantage is still standing.

27.5.call: This was the biggest fight of the game, won 4-1 at our inner tower, and it immediately turned into the Orb Prime taken on our side in the same window. Winning the fight and taking the buffed objective in the same window is exactly the shape of play that closed the game out, though it wasn't every fight — the team only cashed 3 of its 5 won fights into a prize within 90 seconds.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Kira's build ran Tainted Rounds, Ruination, Terminus, Imperator, and Nuclear Rounds instead of two of the meta core's three pieces, Solaris and Ashbringer. Tainted Rounds' 45% healing reduction on-hit answered the heal-stacking threat from Muriel directly, something the kit read for this matchup calls out. What it skipped was the ability-tempo route: Solaris empowers the next basic after every ability cast and heals for half the damage dealt, and Ashbringer refunds cooldowns on-hit, both built to loop Kira's Mercy-into-Purge combo faster rather than just hit harder. The raw damage-and-anti-heal route was enough this game, 14 kills and the roster's highest damage to heroes at 48,265, but it leaned on crit and on-hit power instead of the faster ability uptime the community core is built around.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: The engine's pick for Kira is Vermis, whose major deals bonus damage equal to a slice of the target's max health every third consecutive basic on the same hero, paired with Melting Point for extra damage against heavily armored targets. That's a sustained-trade engine built for exactly what Kira's kit wants: stick on one target through repeated hits rather than one burst window. It trades away a pure item-scaling major, which would reward finishing all five items faster, for a payoff that scales with the length of the fight — a fit for a carry who scored across many separate engagements rather than a single decisive one. This is theoretical; the match feed doesn't record which Eternal was actually equipped.

63523579-8bde-4b3c-bc1a-62ac12f76d52.build: Khaimera's build finished Overlord, Rapture, and Void Helm, replacing the meta core's third piece, Basilisk, with a magic-armor item instead. Void Helm's 45 magical armor and 20% bonus healing from all sources amplify his own health-regen passive directly, and it answered an enemy comp that ran 3 of 5 magical damage. What it gave up was Basilisk's stacking armor shred and flat physical power, a dueling tool built for sticking on one target through a long trade — exactly Khaimera's win condition, but one that needs him alive long enough to land the stacks, and five deaths meant the build never got there. Only three items were completed by the end, the fewest on the roster, so neither route ever got the full six-item payoff.
63523579-8bde-4b3c-bc1a-62ac12f76d52.eternal: The engine's pick for Khaimera is also Vermis, rewarding the same sustained on-hit pattern, which lines up with his win condition of sticking on one target and out-sustaining them through the fight. Melting Point's bonus damage against heavily armored targets would have helped him punch through the enemy frontline he keeps engaging. The trade is a slower-scaling major against a kit that instead needed to survive to use it: Khaimera died five times and never got past three completed items, so the sustained-attack payoff rarely had the time on target to matter. It's theoretical, since the feed doesn't show which Eternal was actually run.

78f6b9bb-653c-46bf-bf03-b3669063b1e9.build: Greystone's build finished Overlord, Tainted Blade, Augmentation, Aegis Of Agawar, and Imperator, keeping two of the meta core's three pieces and skipping Rapture, the omnivamp-and-attack-speed sustain piece, for Tainted Blade's 45% healing reduction instead — one of only two anti-heal items on the roster, and a direct answer to Muriel's heal-stacking kit. Aegis Of Agawar's passive scales 10% of total armor into both physical and magical resistance, rising to 20% below 40% health, but that percentage-based defense was the only magic resistance in the build; nothing carried flat magical armor against a comp running 3 of 5 magical damage, the gap the matchup read flags directly. It never cost Greystone a death this game; the lane was won outright, with only one death across the whole match. Even so, it's the one hole in an otherwise clean build.
78f6b9bb-653c-46bf-bf03-b3669063b1e9.eternal: The engine's pick for Greystone is Thraex, whose major marks whoever he last basic-attacked for a damage-up, damage-down trade window, paired with Ferocity's attack speed that ramps the longer he stays in a fight. That's a sustained-duelist engine that fits a frontline win condition built on soaking damage and resetting fights with a stasis heal. It trades away flat health scaling, the kind a pure tank major offers, for a bigger payoff the longer a single trade runs — a fit for a lane that Greystone won outright, where extended fights favored him. This is theoretical; the feed doesn't record the Eternal actually equipped.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Argus's build finished Azure Core, Combustion, Wraith Leggings, Noxia, and Oblivion Crown, keeping two of the meta core's three pieces and swapping Entropy, a flat damage-on-hit amp built for repeated poke, for Noxia's mark-and-detonate combo that deals 6% of a target's max health once a second ability lands on the mark. That's a burst-against-tanky-targets pick over the meta's steady chip damage, useful against a frontline like Crunch, but it came online late, around minute 30, well after the early lane struggles. The core itself wasn't the problem in those first ten minutes; none of these five items were bought yet. The three solo catches by Neon came while the midlane matchup was still unfavored early, a lane disadvantage itemization alone couldn't have fixed.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: The engine's pick for Argus is Vesh, whose major turns every ability hit on a hero into an added damage-over-time tick, with Mind Rot adding a further slice of the target's current health on top. That rewards exactly Argus's poke-and-zone identity, stacking extra damage onto the multi-ability rotation of Dread Nova, Ether Crystal, and Particle Shredder before the channel ult. It trades away a burst-window major for damage that builds across a longer rotation, which suits a lane that opened lost, three solo catches by Neon before minute 10, but recovered into an even fight built on repeated poke rather than one all-in. It's theoretical, since the feed doesn't record which Eternal actually ran.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Phase's build finished Marshal and Enra's Blessing, the meta core's two protect pieces, but swapped the third, Galaxy Greaves, for Vanguardian, trading Greaves' mobility and jump utility for a flat 75 tenacity and 35 armor of both types instead. Windcaller went in as well, adding a 12% boost to Phase's own heals and shields on top of Enra's ally-shield proc. Against Crunch, the one hard-CC and dive threat the matchup read calls out for the enemy backline, tenacity is a direct answer: it cuts the lockdown Crunch needs to land his combo. That said, it gives up the faster rotations Galaxy Greaves would have offered between fights. The build produced the roster's highest healing total, 18,548, and the most wards placed, 13, backing up the trade.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: The engine's pick for Phase is also Vesh, adding a damage-over-time tick to every ability hit on top of a kit whose passive already heals her and her linked ally off those same casts. That fits her ability-based combo of Telekinetic Link, Psychic Flare, and Energy Lance, even in a game where Phase's actual output stayed low, 11,370 damage to heroes, because the support lane was lost to Muriel the entire game and left little room to poke. The trade-off against a pure peel-and-tank major is real: Vesh pays off on landing abilities on enemies, not on keeping an ally alive, though the 12 assists suggest the peel job got done regardless. This is theoretical; the match feed doesn't record which Eternal was actually equipped.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~1.3s of lockdown): Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Muriel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Dive threat on our backline: Crunch. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Phase) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
ourKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
ourKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Dread Nova stun → Ether Crystal push/lift → Particle Shredder channel → Synaptic Obliterator beams
ourKits.winCondition: poke from max range and zone with the crystal
ourKits.playWith: a frontline to protect his stationary channel
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Dread Nova; dive him during the immobile ult channel

ourKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
ourKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

enemyKits.passive: permanent power on unique hero takedowns
enemyKits.playWith: setup that holds a target for the execute
enemyKits.playAgainst: bait Safeguard's spellshield before committing the key CC
